claims.source_quote_ar: ما كانَ لِيَأْخُذَ أَخاهُ فِي دِينِ الْمَلِكِ
claims.claim_ar: تركيب «ما ... إلا» إعلان للحصر: يقتصر جواب قومه على القول المذكور فقط.
claims.claim_en: The construction 'ما ... إلا' functions as restriction/limitation: it confines the people's answer to that single expressed response.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted source example uses a similar 'ما كان' pattern in another narrative; applying it to this ayah is inferential and should be reviewed against explicit commentary on 'ما ... إلا' in relation to this verse.
claims.rhetorical_effect: limits and sharpens meaning (emphasis by restriction), making the reported answer appear concise and exclusive.

claims.source_quote_ar: لم حذف العاطف من قوله قالَ يا قَوْمِ ولم يقل «فقال»
claims.claim_ar: حذف أداة العطف أو أسلوب الربط في نقل الكلام؛ التقرير المختصر لجواب القوم يقترب من أسلوب حذف العاطف (التقليل من أدوات الربط بين الأقوال).
claims.claim_en: Omission of the coordinating particle (حذف العاطف) in reported speech: the concise report of the people's answer resembles the stylistic omission of connective particles, producing a compact narrative.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source discusses omission of connectives in other prophetic narratives (e.g., 'قال يا قوم') rather than this verse explicitly; mapping that discussion onto this ayah is plausible but interpretative.

claims.source_quote_ar: كأنه قيل: فما قال هود حينئذ؟ قيل: يا قوم
claims.claim_ar: التفتة إلى الكلام المباشر ــ عرض إجابة القوم كما لو أنها رد على سؤال: انتقال من السرد إلى كلام مباشر يؤثر في تلقي القارئ.
claims.claim_en: A shift (iltifat) to direct speech — the people's reply is presented as if answering a question, effecting a shift from narrative summary into quoted utterance.
claims.needs_review_reason: Source shows the same rhetorical technique in related prophetic stories; attribution to this ayah is interpretive and should be cross-checked with exegesis that treats the shift explicitly.
claims.rhetorical_effect: creates immediacy and vividness by simulating direct reply, increasing the force of the reported words.
